calc.loan.faq.6.a: The principal is the amount you borrowed; the interest is what the lender charges for it. Each payment covers that month's interest first and the rest reduces the principal, so the split shifts toward principal over the life of the loan.
calc.student-loan.note.incomeContingent: Repayments here are income-contingent in practice: you pay a share of earnings above a threshold, not a fixed installment, and the balance is written off after the statutory period.
calc.income-tax.faq.2.a: No. This covers the main allowances and the standard deduction. Special reliefs, credits and local taxes are not modeled, so treat the result as an estimate.
calc.income-tax.hint.us: Itemized deductions. They replace the standard deduction only if they exceed it.
calc.income-tax.hint.jp: Insurance premiums, dependents and other deductions.
calc.income-tax.hint.br: Legal deductions, if you itemize instead of taking the simplified allowance.
calc.income-tax.note.fr: 2025 barème for a single share. The quotient familial for couples and dependents is not modeled.
calc.income-tax.note.be: 2025 rates including an indicative 7% communal surcharge. Regional differences are not modeled.
calc.income-tax.note.nl: Box 1 for 2025, below state pension age, with the general and labor tax credits applied.
calc.income-tax.note.pt: Mainland Portugal for 2025, single taxpayer without dependents.
calc.income-tax.note.br: IRPF annualized from the 2025 monthly table using the simplified deduction, plus INSS.
calc.superannuation.note: Uses the 12% Superannuation Guarantee rate from 1 July 2025. Contribution caps and Division 293 tax are not modeled.
calc.30-percent-ruling.note: The exemption applies up to the capped salary. Eligibility, the five-year maximum and the scheduled reduction to 27% are not modeled here.
calc.severance-pay.desc: Calculate severance and notice pay under Turkish labor law.
calc.sip.stepUpHint: Raise the installment by this much every year.
calc.sip.explain.1: Each installment is invested at the start of the month and compounds monthly at the expected rate, so early installments do the heaviest lifting.
conv.length.explain: Every length here is defined against the meter. The imperial units are exact conversions rather than approximations: an inch is defined as 25.4 mm, which makes a foot exactly 0.3048 m.
conv.area.desc: Convert between square meters, feet, acres and hectares.
conv.area.explain: Area units are the square of their length units, which is why the factors are larger than people expect: a square foot is about a tenth of a square meter, not a third.
conv.volume.desc: Convert between liters, milliliters, gallons and cups.
conv.pressure.explain: These are all force over area. Tire pressures are usually quoted as gauge pressure, which is measured relative to the surrounding air rather than to a vacuum.
conv.angle.explain: A full turn is 360 degrees, 2π radians or 400 gradians. Radians are the natural unit in math because the arc length of a unit circle equals the angle.
tool.number-to-words.desc: Spell a number out, the way an amount is written on a check.
chart.length.desc: Meters, centimeters, feet, inches and yards side by side.
chart.area.desc: Square meters, square feet, yards, acres and hectares.
chart.area.explain: Area factors are the square of the length factors, which is why a square foot is about a tenth of a square meter rather than a third.
chart.volume.desc: Liters, milliliters, gallons and cups side by side.
chart.pressure.explain: Useful for tire pressures, which are quoted in bar in Europe and psi in the US. These are gauge pressures, measured relative to the surrounding air.
chart.squares.explain: Squares and cubes come up constantly in area and volume work, and the square roots are the ones worth recognizing on sight.
chart.percentFraction.explain: The same quantity written three ways. Recognizing that 1/8 is 12.5% makes a lot of mental arithmetic faster.

chart.paper.desc: A-series and US paper sizes in millimeters and inches.
chart.paper.note: A-series dimensions are exact; US sizes are given in millimeters converted from their inch definitions.
guide.what-amortisation.title: What Is Amortization?
guide.what-amortisation.intro.1: Amortization is the process of paying a loan off in equal installments, where each payment covers that month's interest first and puts whatever is left toward the balance.
guide.what-amortisation.intro.2: Because interest is charged on the outstanding balance, early payments are mostly interest. As the balance falls, the interest portion shrinks and the principal portion grows, so the loan clears faster and faster toward the end.
guide.what-inflation.note.1: Your personal inflation rate is not the headline one. The published figure is an average across a basket of goods; if your spending is weighted toward rent or energy, your experience can be very different.
guide.compare-loans.intro.2: Comparing properly means holding one thing constant and looking at the total cost rather than the installment.
guide.read-schedule.title: How to Read an Amortization Schedule
guide.read-schedule.intro.1: An amortization schedule lists every payment over the life of a loan, split into the part that covers interest and the part that reduces the balance.
guide.fv.note.1: Of that total, 120,000 is money paid in and the rest is growth. The split shifts heavily toward growth the longer the term runs, which is the whole argument for starting early.

calc.bmi.explain.1: BMI divides your weight in kilograms by the square of your height in meters. The same number is used worldwide, which is why it is a useful common reference even though it is a blunt one.
calc.tdee.explain.2: The lose and gain options shift that by 500 calories a day, which is the usual starting point for roughly half a kilogram a week. Track what actually happens for a two weeks and adjust — the equation is an estimate, your bathroom scale is data.
calc.bodyFat.measureHint: In centimeters, or inches multiplied by 2.54.
calc.pace.explain.1: Pace is time divided by distance — how long each kilometer or mile takes. Speed is the same information the other way round, as distance per hour.
calc.area.note: Units are whatever you put in. Enter meters and the area is square meters; enter feet and it is square feet.
calc.volume.note: Units follow your input. A cubic meter is exactly 1,000 liters, which is what the last row converts.
calc.volume.faq.2.q: How do I get liters or gallons from this?
calc.volume.faq.2.a: Measure in meters and multiply cubic meters by 1,000 for liters, which the last row does. For gallons, take those liters to the volume converter.
calc.breakEven.explain.1: Every unit sold contributes price minus variable cost toward the fixed costs. Break-even is simply fixed costs divided by that contribution.
calc.roi.desc: Return on investment, in total and annualized.
calc.roi.explain.2: The limitation is that it says nothing about time. The annualized figure fixes that by compounding the return back over the holding period, so a 40% gain over three years is comparable with one over five.
calc.roas.explain.2: Break-even ROAS is 1 divided by your gross margin. On a 40% margin you need 2.5× just to stand still, because only 40 of every 100 in revenue was ever available to pay for the ad.
calc.fuelCost.note: Distance, economy and price must be in matching units — miles with gallons, kilometers with liters. Real consumption also varies with speed, load and traffic.
calc.fuelCost.explain.2: That reversal is also why the two cannot be compared directly: more km per liter is better, more liters per 100 km is worse.
calc.fuelCost.faq.2.a: Yes, substantially. A UK imperial gallon is about 4.546 liters against the US gallon's 3.785, so UK mpg figures look roughly 20% better for the same car. The fuel economy converter handles the conversion.
calc.recipe.amountHint: Any quantity from the recipe — grams, milliliters, whatever it uses.
calc.gpa.note: Courses with zero credits are ignored, so you can leave the slots you do not need. This uses the common US 4.0 scale; your institution's own scale may differ, and many weight honors or advanced courses higher.
calc.concrete.note: Units are whatever you entered — meters in, cubic meters out. The constituent split uses the standard 1.54 dry-volume allowance and is an estimate for ordering, not a mix design.
calc.concrete.explain.1: Volume is length × width × thickness, plus a waste allowance for spillage, uneven ground and over-dig. Ten percent is the usual figure; more on rough ground.
calc.concrete.faq.1.a: Bags are practical up to roughly a cubic meter. Beyond that, ready-mix is cheaper, far quicker and more consistent — and a large slab poured in bag-sized batches risks cold joints.
calc.paint.coverageHint: From the can — usually 10–14 m² per liter, or around 350 sq ft per gallon.
calc.paint.note: Coverage falls on porous or previously unpainted surfaces, and a strong color change may need an extra coat. Buying slightly over is usually cheaper than a second trip for a part-tin.
calc.paint.explain.1: Wall area is the perimeter multiplied by the height. Subtract the doors and windows, divide by the coverage on the can, and multiply by the number of coats.
calc.paint.faq.2.a: Two over a similar color. Three when going light over dark, or onto bare plaster, where the first coat is mostly absorbed. A primer or mist coat on new plaster is cheaper than an extra topcoat.
calc.tile.faq.1.a: Slightly, and in your favor — the joints mean each tile covers marginally more than its own size. It is well inside the waste allowance, so it is not worth modeling.
calc.force.explain.1: Newton's second law: F = m × a. One newton is the force that accelerates one kilogram at one meter per second squared.
calc.force.explain.2: Weight is the special case where the acceleration is gravity, so an 80 kg person weighs about 785 N. Kilogram-force is that divided back by gravity, which is why equipment labeled in kgf reads the same as the mass.
calc.torque.note: Lever length is measured from the center of rotation to where the force is applied, not the overall length of the wrench.
calc.torque.explain.1: Torque is force multiplied by the distance from the pivot: τ = F × r. Doubling the wrench length doubles the torque for the same pull, which is why a breaker bar works.
calc.torque.faq.1.a: Because the component along the lever just pushes toward the pivot and does no turning at all. At 90° all of your effort turns the fastener; at 45° only about 71% of it does.
calc.torque.faq.2.a: One newton-meter is about 0.738 pound-feet, so a 100 N·m spec is roughly 74 lb·ft. Torque wrenches are sold calibrated in one or the other, and the conversion is shown above.

tool.coin-flip.explain: Each flip is drawn independently from the same cryptographic generator the dice use. Over many flips the split drifts toward half and half, but it very rarely lands exactly there — which is what a fair coin actually looks like.
